## A path through the foundations

Start with [setup and the self-check](ch00-start-here/index.html), then work through the chapters in order. Each episode pairs runnable examples with predictions, exercises and worked solutions. Each practical chapter ends with a lab and checkpoint; use its key-points page when revising.

If you already use Python, begin with the [solubility EDA](ch01-scientific-python/05-eda-solubility.html) and its data-quality cautions. If you already fit models, check the [cross-validation](ch02-ml-fundamentals/07-cross-validation.html) and [hyperparameter tuning](ch02-ml-fundamentals/08-hyperparameter-tuning.html) lessons before moving to Chapter 3. They establish the rules used by every later comparison.

## What you should be able to deliver

By the end, you can turn a scientific question into a reproducible modelling report: define the prediction target and independent sampling unit, audit and explore the data, establish a baseline, fit preprocessing within validation, tune a finite set of candidates, and evaluate a fixed procedure on held-out data. You can explain its errors, uncertainty and limits without turning a good score into a causal or deployment claim.

Keep the [maths refresher](../appendices/maths-refresher.html), [glossary](../appendices/glossary.html), [reproducibility toolkit](../appendices/reproducibility.html) and [further reading](../appendices/further-reading.html) nearby. The full [roadmap](../index.html#roadmap) shows where these foundations lead into chemistry and biology.
